messages:
IncidentBot: [INCIDENT] sev2 paging: auth-proxy returning intermittent 500 + session TTLs dropping to 0 for a subset of requests. Observed at 2026-03-15T15:03:41Z. Pager: oncall-sre. @here
Alex (SRE): taking lead. I'm oncall. collecting initial scope.
Sara (SecOps): noted unusual pattern — token TTL header = 0 on ~3% of requests to /auth/validate, spikes align with config push at 15:01 UTC.
Mike (Infra): I saw a noisy deploy to auth-proxy-flags-2026 around 15:00, roll forward flagged. Rolling back?
Jess (Engineering): rollback initiated for auth-proxy flags; hold canary at 0% while we triage.
Alex (SRE): good. can someone dump the proxy config diff and recent commits?
Jess (Engineering): grabbing diff now. quick snippet: `+enable_debug_ttl_override=true` accidentally included in staged config. this would set ttl to 0 for debugging.
Sara (SecOps): oh no — that flag also enabled debug logging to s3://redwood-debug-logs/auth-proxy/ with full headers. Potential PII/session-id exposure.
Anu (Customer Success): list of customers making auth calls in that window? I need to triage customer impact.
Mike (Infra): running query against logs index to list distinct customer_id by timestamp window (15:00-15:04).
Mike (Infra): query returns 12 distinct customer_ids, highest traffic from cust-omega and cust-skyline.
Alex (SRE): mitigation steps: 1) disable debug flag (rollback done), 2) stop further log exports to S3, 3) rotate signing key for short-lived tokens, 4) mass-revoke active sessions for affected customers, 5) notify legal/CISO.
Jess (Engineering): rollback completed and flag removed from canary and prod. propagation at 15:06.
IncidentBot: DeployBot: rollback confirmed on auth-proxy [deploy-789].
Sara (SecOps): disabling log export to s3 now — updating logging config to buffer to internal Kinesis instead of direct s3 put.
Mike (Infra): s3 writes paused for prefix auth-proxy/* — lifecycle events stopped at 15:07.
Jess (Engineering): preparing key rotation plan. we have two signing keys in KMS: auth-signing-primary and auth-signing-rotate. I'll schedule rotation and overlap window to avoid mass login failures.
Sara (SecOps): we must assume the debug logs may contain session ids and IPs. Immediate action: rotate token signing keys and revoke refresh tokens issued in window 15:00-15:06.
Alex (SRE): commands to revoke refresh tokens for affected customers (example):
```
# list tokens by customer
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://internal-api.redwood/v1/tokens?customer=cust-omega&issued_after=2026-03-15T15:00:00Z
# bulk revoke
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://internal-api.redwood/v1/tokens/revoke -d '{"customer":"cust-omega","issued_before":"2026-03-15T15:06:00Z"}'
```
Mike (Infra): executing revoke for top 3 impacted customers now (cust-omega, cust-skyline, cust-lumen). I'll kick off script; will provide job id.
Mike (Infra): revoke job started: job-5543. estimated 120s to complete.
Anu (Customer Success): prepping emails to impacted customers. Need to know whether session cookies or tokens were present in logs.
Sara (SecOps): logs likely contain `Authorization: Bearer <token>` in debug dump. Must treat as compromised. Recommend telling customers to rotate any long-lived API keys and informing them of incident.
CISO Bot: Severity uplift recommended to P1 until keys rotated and revocations complete. Confirmed risk of token leakage.
Alex (SRE): agree. escalating to P1 for active mitigation. Notifying on-call security lead.
Jess (Engineering): key rotation steps (outline): 1) generate new signing key in KMS, 2) configure auth-service to accept both keys for 10m, 3) publish new key for token signing, 4) wait 2m to allow token issuance, 5) revoke old key and invalidate tokens signed with it. I'll run commands now.
Jess (Engineering): generated new key: `projects/redwood/kms/keys/auth-rot-205100`. updating config and rolling out.
IncidentBot: Auth Service rollout started: rollout-1122.
Mike (Infra): rotation applying. auth-service configured to accept both keys. new tokens being issued as of 15:12.
Mike (Infra): revoke job finished job-5543: success, revoked ~18k refresh tokens across affected customers.
Sara (SecOps): proceeding to schedule KMS key disable for old key in 10 minutes to allow outstanding short-lived tokens to expire. We'll mark old key disabled at 15:22.
Alex (SRE): confirm no ongoing 500s?
Jess (Engineering): 500s returned to baseline. proxy latency normalized.
Anu (Customer Success): drafts ready for customers. requesting final wording: we rotated keys and revoked impacted refresh tokens — recommend customers rotate any long-lived secrets.
CISO Bot: legal notified, incident ticket INC-205100 opened, data exfiltration assessment in progress.
Alex (SRE): follow-ups: - full audit of s3 debug bucket, snapshot exports, correlate any external access; - rotate service tokens that used same logging pipeline; - postmortem to include change in config review process.
Sara (SecOps): tagging evidence and retaining debug dumps in isolated bucket `s3://redwood-sec-evidence/auth-proxy-205100` with restricted access for forensics.
Mike (Infra): I will lock down the original debug bucket and trigger an object-level inventory.
Jess (Engineering): adding pre-commit check to disallow `enable_debug_ttl_override` on prod branches.
Anu (Customer Success): sent initial notifications to top-affected customers. will follow up with individual call for enterprise accounts.
Alex (SRE): handing off to day-shift SRE at 15:40. oncall rotation: @day-sre please take post-mitigation watch, check for token errors and customer escalations.
Day-SRE (via thread): acknowledged, I'm taking watch for next 4 hours. will post status updates every 30m.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation complete, keys rotated, revocations done, export paused. Downgrading to sev2 for watch at 16:05.
Alex (SRE): quick note for postmortem: timeline, root cause (debug flag went to prod), gaps in review, and customer impact summary. Assigning owners: Jess (fix), Sara (forensics), Mike (infra lock), Anu (customer comms).
Jess (Engineering): will produce root-cause PR and link.
Sara (SecOps): evidence collection complete, handing off to forensic analyst.
Anu (Customer Success): customers acknowledged, two enterprise customers requested scheduled call — arranging 1:1.
Alex (SRE): thanks team. closing primary thread at 16:08 after handoff. will update incident ticket with notes. :thumbsup:
